violations.message: RiskReport must link at least one evidence id.

input_narrative: SYNTHETIC NARRATIVE: Synthetic device validation lab reported that the device failed to flag a clinically significant ventricular tachycardia episode in real time. A retrospective clinician review confirms a single missed, sustained ventricular tachycardia episode that self-resolved with no recorded adverse outcome; no second occurrence has yet been confirmed. The device confidence-score log, the retrospective clinician read, and the raw waveform export are all consistent.

claim_support.claim: Missed detection of a clinically significant ventricular tachycardia episode represents a serious potential patient safety risk.
The event triggers obligations under EU MDR Annex I, Section 17.2 regarding software development lifecycle and cybersecurity.
claim_support.support_note: Explicitly states requirements for devices incorporating software.

claim_support.claim: The event triggers obligations under 21 CFR §820.10(c) concerning design controls.
claim_support.support_note: Applies to devices automated with computer software.

claim_support.claim: The event triggers obligations under EU MDR Annex I, Section 17.1 regarding repeatability and reliability.
claim_support.support_note: Requires ensuring performance in line with intended use.

risk_report.rationale: The device failed to correctly identify a clinically significant ventricular tachycardia episode in real time, resulting in a missed detection. While the event self-resolved and no adverse outcome was recorded, this represents a serious potential patient safety risk as sustained ventricular tachycardia can be life-threatening if not promptly addressed. The consistency of the confidence score log, clinician read, and waveform export suggests a systemic issue rather than an isolated anomaly. This necessitates investigation to determine the root cause and prevent recurrence.  The device incorporates software, triggering obligations under EU MDR Annex I, Section 17.2 regarding software development lifecycle and cybersecurity, as well as 21 CFR §820.10(c) concerning design controls for devices automated with computer software. Furthermore, MDR Annex I, Section 17.1 requires that electronic programmable systems ensure repeatability, reliability, and performance in line with their intended use, and that appropriate means are adopted to mitigate risks in the event of a single fault condition.
